# tenzir_api_key (Resource)

A user API key, presented as the `x-tenzir-api-key` header. Its policy restricts the key further; the owner's own permissions still limit every request. Destroying the resource revokes the key, and the platform keeps a record of it.

Needs `User.createApiKey` on the owner, and `ApiKey.read`, `ApiKey.setPolicy`, `ApiKey.rename` and `ApiKey.revoke` on the key.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# A key that may only list its owner's API keys.
resource "tenzir_api_key" "ci" {
  name = "ci"
  policy = jsonencode([
    [{ target = { _tag = "User" }, relationships = ["self"] }, ["User.listApiKeys"]],
  ])
}

output "ci_api_key" {
  value     = tenzir_api_key.ci.key
  sensitive = true
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `name` (String) The display name; must not be blank.
- `policy` (String) What the key may do, as JSON: an array of `[constraints, actions]` pairs, such as `[[{"target":{"_tag":"Workspace"},"relationships":[]},["Workspace.read"]]]`. The platform normalizes policies, merging grants with equal constraints and dropping actions a broader grant covers; a policy that normalizes alike shows no difference. Use `jsonencode` to write one. An empty array `[]` allows only account introspection.

### Optional

- `user_id` (String) The ID of the user who owns the key. Defaults to the user the provider authenticates as.

### Read-Only

- `created_at` (String) When the key was minted.
- `id` (String) The key ID.
- `key` (String, Sensitive) The secret key. The platform returns it only when it mints the key, so it is null after an import.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# <user ID>/<key ID>. The secret key stays unknown after an import.
terraform import tenzir_api_key.ci 01a1a205-9e50-7d13-bac1-3f47f9cc4297/6be150e4-e581-4c34-81fc-a8074ceebbd9
```
